item_taken.why: The return rests on a vacancy Kestrel has not re-planned (a headcount line), and it expires at Kestrel's next planning cycle (the 15 October lock, drawn up without reference to her) with no one declining, no one asked, and employment afterwards a new hire from outside, which is this item's condition lost (a capability on the counterparty's side), carrier (the planning cadence), and last intervention (a dated return or a reservation the cycle must respect, which she never sent); not Landlord changes, since the counterparty stays and only the shape goes, and not Standstill with a term, since no paper with a date was written to hold the return open.

reasoning: The rule has two conjuncts and both hold. The deadline belongs to a party elsewhere: 15 October is Kestrel's headcount lock, a counterparty's planning cycle that no one at the Ostrava table owns or can move. It was brought to the table as the holder's alternative: on 20 August she wrote to Ostrava 'settle the level before then or I go back', and leverage rode on it, since Ostrava conceded the level on 9 October and recorded it as 'granted against the Kestrel return'. The rule's residual clause, that a clock stays here only when no party's leverage rides on it, is therefore not met, so the rule places the case on walkaway-manufactures' side as Absent owner's clock. The rule decides on the deadline's ownership and its use at the table; it does not turn on whether the alternative was later exercised, so the fact that the return lapsed on 15 October unexercised and the contract issued on 20 November at the conceded level travels with the case as fact rather than deciding the crossing.
case_out: Ines Farro, a senior engineer negotiating an offer from Ostrava Labs in August 2026, borrowed as her alternative to Ostrava's table a return to Kestrel Systems, from which she had been on open-ended unpaid leave since 1 September 2025 under an undated letter promising an equivalent post. The alternative's existence was held in another party's calendar: the post existed only as a line in Kestrel's headcount plan, which locks every 15 October and is drawn up without reference to her, so the deadline she brought to Ostrava was Kestrel's and not hers or Ostrava's. On 20 August 2026 she wrote to Ostrava: 'Kestrel's plan locks on 15 October and my post lapses with it; settle the level before then or I go back.' Ostrava conceded the level on 9 October 2026, wrote it into the draft offer, and noted in its offer file that the level was 'granted against the Kestrel return', but its contract could not issue until an export-control screening completing on 18 November. She sent Kestrel nothing between 20 August and 15 October. On 15 October 2026 Kestrel's plan folded her line into two existing posts; no one at Kestrel had organized a use for her desk, the two engineers taking her duties had not asked for them, no one was asked about her, and no one opposed or declined her return, which became unexercisable, since employment at Kestrel afterwards would be a new hire from outside. She never returned to Kestrel. On 20 November 2026 she signed Ostrava's contract at the level conceded on 9 October, five weeks after the alternative it was conceded against had stopped existing.
